alex: Quick heads-up — noticed a throughput regression on qwen-mqa after the kernel swap from matmul_v1 -> matmul_v2_fast. 8k seq synthetic workload, p99 latency is fine but overall tok/s dropped ~18%.
maria: ugh. can you paste numbers? which bench (single-stream or async)?
alex: async single-host, batcher config: max_batch_tokens=4096, batching_window_ms=6. Baseline (matmul_v1): 1200 tok/s. After swap: 985 tok/s.
ryan: that is sizable. did membandwidth or L1/L2 counters change? could be more cache churn with MQA layout.
alex: perf counters from the run:
```
Kernel matmul_v1: L1-miss=12.4%, L2-miss=4.8%, DRAM_bw=520GB/s
Kernel matmul_v2_fast: L1-miss=19.1%, L2-miss=6.3%, DRAM_bw=610GB/s
```
alex: flamegraph snapshot (very small):
```
matmul_v2_fast   |████████████████████████████████
kv_cache_evict   |███████
kv_lookup        |████████████
batcher_wait     |██
```
sasha: KV eviction spike looks suspicious. Any change in evict thresholds or alignment when we moved to the new kernel? Could be causing paged-KV fragmentation and extra DMA.
maria: checked model config: qwen-mqa (num_key_value_heads=32, kv_dim=128 per head) unchanged. But kernel change also altered memory alignment for tile width -> introduced 64-byte misalignment for our KV slab header.
ryan: that misalignment explains extra L1 misses and higher DRAM BW. If evict heuristics are sensitive to header reads, we may be walking more pages.
alex: repro script attached (snippet):
```
# repro seq=8192
./bench_infer --model qwen-mqa --seq 8192 --kernel matmul_v2_fast \
  --batcher-max-tokens 4096 --warmup 200 --steps 500
```
alex: after instrumenting cache evict path, we see frequent partial-page evicts (~37% of evicts touch <50% of page) whereas baseline had ~11%.
sasha: partial-page evicts => fragmentation. Paged-KV allocator assumed 256B header alignment. If kernel changed layout to 64B, free list fragmentation will increase.
maria: two short mitigations:
- revert kernel in canary hosts to matmul_v1 (fast rollback)
- short-term: increase evict_coalesce_threshold from 0.75 -> 0.92 so we keep pages around until more fills
ryan: long-term we should either adapt allocator to alignment-agnostic headers or change kernel memory stride back. I'd prefer allocator fix so other kernels don't break.
alex: tried changing evict_coalesce_threshold on a canary: throughput improved to 1125 tok/s (from 985), L1-miss down to 14.9%, DRAM_bw 540GB/s. Still not full baseline but much better.
sasha: that's promising. Also, consider tweaking num_key_value_heads mapping: when heads are split across pages badly, per-head strides cause scattered loads. For qwen-mqa we can try num_key_value_heads=16 (keep kv_dim per head doubled) to test layout compaction.
maria: test matrix proposed:
1) rollback kernel (control)
2) evict_threshold tweak only
3) head-folding (32->16) only
4) both tweaks
alex: I ran (3) on test cluster: num_key_value_heads=16 gave 1180 tok/s with matmul_v2_fast. So head-folding recovers most perf; suggests head packing reduces scatter.
ryan: good datapoint. We need to watch quality — folding heads may affect attention math (we're reinterpreting dims) — ensure tests compare logits/embeddings within tolerance.
sasha: as a follow-up, I'll file an allocator PR to use header-size-agnostic metadata and implement a small compaction pass on free-list merges. Also add a health metric for partial-page-evict-rate.
infra-bot: deploy proposal created -> rollback-canary-2345678910 (status: pending)
maria: plan: 1) roll back kernel on 10% canary (infra action) 2) apply evict_threshold tweak on 10% 3) run head-folding perf+quality tests (qa/bench)
alex: assignment: sasha -> allocator PR + metric (ETA 48h). ryan -> perf regression postmortem writeup. maria -> coordinate canary rollback + perf runs. I'll open the bench artifacts in the thread.
sasha: ack. starting allocator patch now.
alex: attaching small perf log excerpt and diff of allocator counters for triage in the PR.
alex: final note — this was a good catch: kernel micro-optimizations can alter memory layout assumptions downstream. we should add a kernel-change checklist item: "verify allocator header alignment invariants and run kv-frag-smokebench" :eyes:
maria: agreed. adding to release checklist. :white_check_mark:
ryan: thanks all. tagging @eng-sre for canary ops.
infra-bot: rollback-canary-2345678910 -> started on hosts [canary-03, canary-07]
alex: will follow up with a short postmortem once sasha's PR lands.
